paragraphs: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. (a) In Mishnah Avot, chapter 4. Further Mishnah references (chapter:mishnah): Kilayim 2:9;4:8;5:3;6:2. Shevi'it 2:10. Terumot 3:5. Bikkurim 1:5. Shabbat 8:6;15:2. Eruvin 6:1;8:10. Shekalim 6:3. Mo'ed Katan 1:3. Yevamot 13:3. Nedarim 3:1;5:1,2. Sotah 9:4. Kiddushin 4:7. Makkot 2:2. Menachot 5:6;9:3. Bekhorot 3:1. Arakhin 2:6. Keritot 2:1. Tamid 5:2. Middot 1:2,9;2:5,6;5:4. Kelim 7:3;28:9. Nega'im 7:1;10:4;11:11. Parah 9:2. Makhshirin 6:3. Tohorot 3:8. Eruvin, beginning of Haddar, and 88a; Shabbat 81a.

(b) He lived long, from the Temple’s time to later generations. His mother’s brother was a Levite in the Temple, Middot, chapter 1; tractate Middot was composed on his authority. He was one of Akiva’s seven students established after twenty-four thousand died (see Akiva), Bereshit Rabbah, Vayyosef Avraham. At persecution’s end, our masters gathered in Usha, including Eliezer ben Yaakov, Shir Hashirim Rabbah. Yuchasin quotes the gloss Master Moshe Isserles made to Yesod Olam’s chain of tradition: “Yochanan ben Zakkai received from Hillel and Shammai. His students: Eliezer, Yehoshua,” etc.; “his colleagues: Eliezer ben Yaakov and Tzadok,” etc. See Yuchasin, chronological section under those sages. Be'er Sheva, Eglah Arufah 45b, Mishnah: “Whence does he measure? Akiva: from the nose; Eliezer ben Yaakov: from the neck.” Maimonides rules like Akiva. Kesef Mishneh: “Surprising, since Eliezer ben Yaakov’s teaching is ‘a kav, but clean.’ He must hold that this rule does not override the rule favoring Akiva against his colleague.” End quotation. Be'er Sheva objects: Eliezer ben Yaakov was not Akiva’s colleague. He was of Yochanan ben Zakkai’s generation, who saw the destruction, whereas Akiva and his colleagues were afterward. Listing Akiva first is unsurprising: the Passover Haggadah puts him before his teacher Tarfon, as Ketubbot shows; many places put student before teacher. End quotation. Brother, see how those two great luminaries erred in what they saw! Yuchasin’s compiler forgot his own Bereshit Rabbah citation—Chayyei Sarah, section 61—and Tanchuma, end of Chayyei Sarah, which make Eliezer ben Yaakov Akiva’s student. Likewise Yevamot 93a: Eliezer ben Yaakov follows Akiva; see Rashi and Tosafot on b, “after,” and Rabbi Yannai Rabbah. Tosafot, Bava Batra 79, end of b, likewise call him Akiva’s student. Akiva was Eliezer the great’s student, and Eliezer was Yochanan ben Zakkai’s student; see their entries, explicit countless times in the Talmud. How could Eliezer ben Yaakov be Zakkai’s colleague, a student of his student’s student? He also taught Meir, Yevamot and the above Rashi/Tosafot; Meir was Akiva’s student. Thus he lived in Meir’s days after Akiva. Yalkut, Mattot, section 785, Sifrei Zuta on “On the day he hears”: Eliezer ben Yaakov said, “I asked Yonatan ben Meshullam and Yehoshua ben Gamla whence,” etc.; “They said, Akiva said,” etc.; “When I came to Yehoshua,” etc.; “I asked Rabbi Yonatan ben Meshullam and Yehoshua ben Mammal,” etc. Nazir 56b: Yehoshua bar Mammal learned from Yehoshua (see there), Zakkai’s student. More: Kilayim, chapter 4, has Eliezer ben Yaakov report Chananya ben Chakhinai, Akiva’s student (see there). He reports an Akiva student. He joined Meir, Yehudah, Yose, Shimon, Nechemyah, and Yochanan Hassandlar to intercalate the year, likewise Akiva’s student (see there). He spoke in Meir’s name, Chullin 38. See Yehudah bar Ilai, with whom he was in Usha. There Tosafot say Yehudah did not see Zakkai; presumably neither did Eliezer ben Yaakov, listed after Yehudah and Nechemyah (see there), Meir, Yose, Shimon bar Yochai, Elazar son of Yose, and Eliezer ben Yaakov. Zakkai died three or four years after the destruction; Akiva was killed seventy-three years afterward. Even granting Eliezer ben Yaakov lived into the generation after Akiva, he could hardly be a colleague in Zakkai’s old age. They are mistaken. Maimonides rightly favors Akiva over him: the law follows Akiva even against colleagues, all the more against a student.

(c) They found written in a book in Jerusalem, “Eliezer ben Yaakov’s teaching is a kav, but clean,” Gittin 67a. Rashi: the law always follows him; Eruvin 36, 62b; Yevamot 37b, see Rashi, and 49, 60a; Bekhorot 23b. Maginnei Shlomo, beginning of Pesachim: even against a majority, as Yevamot 37, 60; apparently even against an anonymous ruling, etc. His Yevamot novellae ask whether even against an anonymous Mishnah: Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, says Eliezer ben Yaakov holds one transgresses after two festivals; Maimonides, Ma'aseh Hakkorbanot, chapter 14, requires three. Difficult, since the kav-and-clean rule applies even to a baraita, Yevamot 60a. Perhaps not against an anonymous Mishnah. See Semag, negative commandment 331. End quotation; see there. See Responsa P.M., part II, section 119 [פ״מ; work unresolved], why sometimes the law does not follow him. Chacham Tzvi, section 10: the rule against a student opposing his teacher prevails over kav-and-clean, because it applies to all students, and Eliezer ben Yaakov was Akiva’s student. She'erit Yosef 39a cites Rosh, Mi Shehotzi'uhu and Bakkol Me'arvin, a gloss to Sefer Keritot, and Mordekhai, Mi Shehotzi'uhu: in 102 places the law follows him; the above Yevamot passage troubles him, see there. Ran, Shevuot, chapter 1: only against one person. Tosafot, Nedarim 23b: if the sages disagree with him, does the law follow them? … Sometimes we rule against him. Perhaps Maimonides agrees; this removes Tosafot Yom Tov’s difficulty on Kilayim 2:9, 4:8; see Eruvin 8:10 and Tosafot there. Rosh, Halakhot Ketannot, laws of impurity, disagrees: there is no distinction. See Rosh, Nedarim, chapter 3: Rav does not accept this rule. Kav-and-clean is not confined to the Mishnah; it applies in a baraita too, as Tosafot, Kiddushin 62, end of b: “Though generally we favor Eliezer ben Yaakov as kav-and-clean, here neither his view nor the tannaim allowing transfer of what has not yet come into existence is law. Rav Nachman rejects that transfer, and the law follows him in civil cases.” End quotation. See above whether kav-and-clean overrides another rule, etc. His transfer statement is a baraita, not Mishnah, yet they invoke kav-and-clean. Were it inapplicable to baraitot, his baraita would already be rejected without the rule favoring Rav Nachman. Thus ‘his teaching’ includes baraita. Its context proves it: Shimon ben Azzai found this written long before Rabbi arranged the Mishnah. Earlier too there were orders of Mishnah: Chagigah says Yehudah ben Tema and colleagues studied six hundred orders. Yose, Rabbi’s teacher, ends Kelim, “Happy are you, Kelim, entering in impurity and emerging in purity.” Clearly Rabbi added and removed. Since kav-and-clean predates his arrangement, it cannot refer to his particular Mishnah collection, there, Responsa Chacham Tzvi. Rashbam, Bava Batra 138a, says so explicitly. See Tosafot, Ketubbot 109a, and Menachot 31b. Chavvot Yair: one cannot prove ‘Mishnah’ is imprecise merely because he is not mentioned 102 times in our Mishnah; the tannaim may have had many more mishnayot, as Chagigah says. End quotation. On Maimonides favoring Shimon bar Yochai over him, see there. Tosafot, Gittin 52b: Rabbenu Tam says the law does not follow Eliezer ben Yaakov despite ‘the law follows him’ and kav-and-clean, since one does not learn practical law from a Talmudic report; see there. Ellu Kesharim rules like him: an explicit ruling was needed, implying the general rule is insufficient.

(d) Tanna de-Vei Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, Eruvin 54a; Chagigah 17b; Sanhedrin 92, end of b; “Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov’s school taught,” beginning of Chelek. A student of his incurred heavenly punishment by burning; they said, “Leave him, for he served a great man.” See Elazar ben Pedat. His student fell ill and forgot his learning; he prayed for him, Devarim Rabbah, chapter 8. Eliezer kav-and-clean’s burial is at Kefar Anan (see Chalafta of Kefar Chananya).

(e) Abba Bira'ah, son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov [בראב״י; reading provisional]—requires examination. Ilai the elder came to him. Elazar ben Antigonus in his name. Elazar Chisma spoke to him. In Chananya ben Chakhinai’s name (see there). He spoke to Yehudah, Pesachim 2b, and disputes with him, Rosh Hashanah 12b; Yochanan Hassandlar (see there). Rabbi Yochanan in his name; Rabbi Yose b.Ch. [ב״ח; patronym unresolved] in his name. Abba Yose ben Chanan in his time. Rabbi Yose testified in his name. Meir, his student (see there), and in Meir’s name. In Pinchas ben Yair’s name, Shocher Tov, section 32. Rabbi Pinchas in his name. Abba Shaul disputes with him.
